sentences.text: The principal building blocks of TTCN-3 are modules.
A module may define a fully executable test suite or just a library.
A module may refer to the TTCN-3 language version and to package versions being used.
A module contains definitions.
NOTE: The term test suite is synonymous with a complete set of TTCN-3 modules containing test cases and a control function.

The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.
A module is defined with the keyword module.
NOTE 1: The treatment of TTCN-3 modules in files, repositories and alike is outside the scope of the present document.

module ModuleIdentifier [ language FreeText { "," FreeText } ] "{"
     [ ModuleDefinitionsPart ]
  "}"
A TTCN-3 module groups a set of (typically cohesive) TTCN-3 definitions.
TTCN-3 modules have an explicit import interface to use definitions from other TTCN-3 or non-TTCN-3 modules.
It is possible to hide definitions in a TTCN-3 module (see clause 8.2.5).
TTCN-3 modules can be compiled/interpreted separately.
They are reusable and parameterizable.
Module names are of the form of a TTCN-3 identifier.
NOTE 2: The module identifier is the informal text name of the module.
In addition, a module specification can carry an optional attribute identified by the language keyword that identifies the edition of the TTCN-3 language, in which the module is specified.
The following language strings are to be used:

"TTCN-3:2001" - to be used with modules complying with V1.1.2 [i.17] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2003" - to be used with modules complying with V2.2.1 [i.18] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2005" - to be used with modules complying with V3.1.1 [i.19] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2007" - to be used with modules complying with V3.2.1 [i.20] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2008" - to be used with modules complying with V3.3.2 [i.21] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2008 Amendment 1" - to be used with modules complying with V3.4.1 [i.22] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2009" - to be used with modules complying with V4.1.1 [i.23] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2010" - to be used with modules complying with V4.2.1 [i.24] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2011" - to be used with modules complying with V4.3.1 [i.25] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2012" - to be used with modules complying with V4.4.1 [i.26] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2013" - to be used with modules complying with V4.5.1 [i.27] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2014" - to be used with modules complying with V4.6.1 [i.28] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2015" - to be used with modules complying with V4.7.1 [i.29] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2016" - to be used with modules complying with V4.8.1 [i.30] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2017" - to be used with modules complying with V4.9.1 [i.31] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2018" - to be used with modules complying with V4.10.1 [i.32] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2019" - to be used with modules complying with V4.11.1 [i.33] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2020" - to be used with modules complying with V4.12.1 [i.34] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2021" - to be used with modules complying with V4.13.1 [i.35] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2022" - to be used with modules complying with V4.14.1 [i.36] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2023" - to be used with modules complying with the present document.
Furthermore, the optional attribute identified by the language keyword may identify package versions being used by this module.

The package tags are defined in ETSI ES 202 781 [i.11], ETSI ES 202 782 [i.14], ETSI ES 202 784 [i.12], ETSI ES 202 785 [i.13], ETSI ES 202 786 [i.37], ETSI ES 203 022 [i.38], and ETSI ES 203 790 [i.39].
The language identifier and the package identifier are to be written as a comma-separated list.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) At most one language string per module shall be given to define the core language version in which the module is defined.
b) Per extension package, at most one extension package string of that extension package shall be used by a module.

module MyTestSuite language "TTCN-3:2003"
  { … }
The module definitions part specifies the top-level definitions of the module and may import visible identifiers from other modules.
Visibility rules are given in clause 8.2.5.
Scope rules for declarations made in the module definitions part and imported declarations are given in clause 5.3.
Those language elements which may be defined in a TTCN-3 module are listed in table 1.
Every definition can be associated with attributes using the with statement defined in clause 27.
Visible module definitions may be imported by other modules.

{ 
     [ Visibility ] (
       TypeDef |
       ConstDef |
       TemplateDef |
       ModuleParDef |
       FunctionDef |
       SignatureDef |
       TestcaseDef |
       AltstepDef |
       ImportDef |
       GroupDef |
       ExtFunctionDef |
       FriendDef |
       ModuleControlDef
     ) [ WithStatement ] 
     [ ";" ]
  }+
Definitions in the module definitions part may be made in any order.
Module definitions can be evaluated at runtime and can be evaluated in any order.
A definition shall be evaluated latest before the first reference to it.
NOTE: If a definition is not used, it may not be evaluated at all.
Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.
They may be used elsewhere in the module.
This includes identifiers imported from other modules.
Declarations of dynamic language elements such as variables or timers shall only be made in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types.
TTCN-3 does not support the declaration of variables in the module definitions part, i.e. global variables cannot be defined in TTCN-3.
However, variables defined in a test component type may be used by all test cases, functions, etc. running on components of that component type.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5.
Module parameters are values or templates that may be supplied by the test environment at runtime.
Module parameters do not change during test execution.
They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.

[ Visibility ] modulepar [ TemplateModifier ]
     [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ]
     { Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] "," }
     Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] ";"
Module parameters behave as global constants or unparameterized templates at runtime.
For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.
Module parameters allow to customize a TTCN-3 test suite for a specific IUT, test setup or test campaign.
It is allowed to specify a default value or template for each module parameter as part of the modulepar declaration.

If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.
The type of the module parameter is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.
When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
If functions are used for the initialization of module parameters, it is strongly advised to adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
Not following these rules may cause non-deterministic test executions.
Visible module parameters can be imported.
Optional fields of record and set module parameters or module parameter fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or a module parameter field, an
optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or
via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.
b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
c) A module parameter shall only be of type address if the address type is explicitly defined within the associated module.
d) Module parameters shall be declared within the module definition part only.
e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).

f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.
If no TemplateModifier is present, the TemplateBody shall resolve to a value.
g) Module parameters shall not be used in type or array definitions.
h) All sub-elements of component or default type of a default value of a module parameter shall be initialized with the special value null.
i) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.
In the module definitions part, definitions can be collected in named groups.
Grouping is done to aid readability and to add logical structure to the module if required.
If necessary, the dot notation shall be used to identify sub-groups within the group hierarchy uniquely, e.g. for the import of a specific sub-group.
A group of definitions can be specified wherever a single definition is allowed.
Groups may be nested, i.e. groups may contain other groups.
This allows the test suite specifier to structure, among other things, collections of test data or functions describing test behaviour.
Groups and nested groups have no scoping.
However, attributes given to a group by an associated with statement apply to all elements of a group (see clause 27).
Import statements may import groups so that all visible elements of a group are imported (see clause 8.2.3.3).
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) Group identifiers across the whole module need not necessarily be unique.
However, top-level group identifiers and all group identifiers of subgroups of a single group shall be unique.
b) Only public visibility can be defined for groups as they are always public.
It is possible to re-use visible definitions specified in different modules using the import statement.
Every definition in a TTCN-3 module has an associated visibility, which is by default public (see clause 8.2.5).
NOTE: Groups are public only.
Importing a group means that only the visible elements of the group are being imported.
An import statement can be used anywhere in the module definitions part.

[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId [-> LocalModuleName]
     ( 
       ( all [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] ) 
       |
       ( "{" ImportSpec "}" )
     )
  [ ";" ]

TTCN-3 supports the import of the following definitions: module parameters, user defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and test cases.

Each definition has a name (defines the identifier of the definition, e.g. a function name), a specification (e.g. a type specification or a signature of a function) and in the case of functions, altsteps and test cases an associated behaviour description.
In addition, import statements of one module can be explicitly imported by another module (see clause 8.2.3.7).
Only definitions or import statements visible from the importing module can be imported (see clause 8.2.5).
In contrast to module definitions, which are by default public, import statements are by default private.
EXAMPLE 1a:
Col1: function; Name: f_myFunction; Specification: (inout MyType1 p_myPar) return MyType2 runs on MyCompType; Behaviour description: { const MyType3 c_myConst := …; : // further behaviour }
Col1; Name; Specification; Behaviour description
Col1: type; Specification: record; Name: MyRecordType; Specification: { MyType4 field1, integer field2 }
Col1; Specification; Name; Specification

field1 := 1,
 field2 := c_myConst, // c_myConst is a module constant
 field3 := PX_ModulePar // PX_ModulePar is module parameter
}

Col1: template; Specification: MyType5; Name: m_myTemplate; Specification: := { field1 := 1, field2 := c_myConst, // c_myConst is a module constant field3 := PX_ModulePar // PX_ModulePar is module parameter }
Col1; Specification; Name; Specification

Behaviour descriptions have no effect on the import mechanism, because their internals are considered to be invisible to the importer when the corresponding functions, altsteps or test cases are imported.
Thus, they are not considered in the following descriptions.

The specification part of an importable definition contains local definitions (e.g. field names of structured type definitions or values of enumerated types) and referenced definitions (e.g. references to type definitions, templates, constants or module parameters).
For the examples above, this means:

**Name** **Local definitions** **Referenced definitions** `function` f_myFunction p_myPar MyType1, MyType2, MyCompType `type` MyRecordType field1, field2 MyType4, integer `template` m_myTemplate MyType5, field1, field2, field3, c_myConst, PX_ModulePar
NOTE 1: The local definitions column refers to identifiers only that are newly defined in the importable definition.

Values assigned to individual fields of importable definitions, e.g. in template definitions, may also be considered as local definitions, but they are not important for the explanation of the import mechanism.
NOTE 2: The referenced definitions field1, field2 and field3 of template MyTemplate are the field names of MyType5, i.e. they are referenced via MyType5.

Referenced definitions are also importable definitions, i.e. the source of a referenced definition can again be structured into a name and a specification part and the specification part also contains local and referenced definitions.
In other words, an importable definition may be built up recursively from other importable definitions.
The TTCN-3 import mechanism is related to the local and referenced definitions used in the specification part of the importable definitions.

The TTCN-3 import mechanism distinguishes between the identifier of a referenced definition and the information _necessary for the usage of a referenced definition within the imported definition.
For the usage, the identifier of a_ referenced definition is not required and therefore not imported automatically.
EXAMPLE 1b: Differentiation between information necessary for the usage and the identifier
If an imported definition has attributes (defined by means of a with statement) then the attributes shall also be imported.
The mechanism to change attributes of imported definitions is explained in clause 27.1.3.
NOTE 3: If the module has global attributes they are associated to definitions without these attributes.
The use of import on single definitions, groups of definitions, definitions of the same kind, etc. may lead to situations where the same definition is referred to more than once.
Such cases shall be resolved by the system and definitions shall be imported only once.
NOTE 4: The mechanisms to resolve such ambiguities, e.g. overwriting and sending warnings to the user, are outside the scope of the present document and should be provided by TTCN-3 tools.
All import statements and definitions within import statements are considered to be treated independently one after the other in the order of their appearance.
All TTCN-3 modules shall have their own name space in which all definitions shall be uniquely identified.
Name _clashes may occur due to import, e.g. import from different modules.

Name clashes shall be resolved using qualified_ name(s) for the imported definition(s), i.e. prefixing the imported definition (which causes the name clash) by the identifier of the module in which it has been defined; the prefix and the identifier shall be separated by a dot (".").

If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

There is one exception to this rule: when in the context of an enumerated type (see clause 6.2.4), an enumerated value is clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module, the enumerated value shall take precedence and the definition in the importing module shall be referenced by using its qualified name (see example 5 below in this clause).
In cases where there are no ambiguities the prefixing need not (but may) be present when the imported definitions are used.
When the definition is referenced in the same module where it is defined, the module identifier of the module (the current module) also may be used for prefixing the identifier of the definition.
For the latter case, prefixing shall only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.
It is allowed to rename a module name during its import.
The new name will be visible only in the importing module.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.
b) Only top-level visible definitions of a module may be imported.
Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.
c) A definition is imported together with its name and all local definitions.

NOTE 5: A local definition, e.g. a field name of a user-defined record type or an enumerated value, has only meaning in the context of the definitions in which it is defined, e.g. a field name of a record type can only be used to access a field of the record type and not outside this context.
In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

d) A definition is imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions (see clause 8.2.5).

NOTE 6: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type reference defined in module A, the corresponding information necessary for the usage of that type is automatically imported into module C (see example 6 below in this clause).
Identifiers of referenced definitions are not automatically imported.

In particular, if module C imports global value or template definitions (e.g. constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (e.g. formal parameters of templates, functions, etc. or constants and variables of component types) of an enumerated type from module B, the enumerated values of this type (i.e. the identifiers) are implicitly and automatically imported to module C. That is, the enumerated values are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C (e.g. when an actual parameter is passed or a value is assigned to a component variable).
Note that this implicit importing does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in module C.

e) If the referenced definitions are wished to be used in the importing module, they shall be explicitly imported either directly from its source module or indirectly by importing the import statements of a module importing it (see clause 8.2.3.7).
f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.
g) The language specification (see clause 8.1) of the import statement shall not override the language specification of the importing module.

h) The language specification of the import statement shall be identical to the language specification of the source module from which definitions are imported (see clause 8.2.3.8) provided a language specification is defined in the source module.
If not, the language specification in the import statement is taken as the language specification of the source module.
If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.
i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.
The imported module can be referenced using the new local name only.
j) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module shall be unique in the scope of the importing module.

Single visible definitions can be imported by referring to the definition kind and the definition name(s).

The import of single definitions can be used in combination with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) 
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]
See clause 8.2.3.
Import of an invisible definition shall cause an error.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.
b) See the restrictions given in clause 8.2.3.
Groups of definitions may be imported.

The import of groups can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).
It is allowed to import sub-groups (i.e. a group which is defined within another group) directly, i.e. without the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.

If the name of a sub-group that should be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module (see clause 8.2.2), the dot notation shall be used to identify the sub-group to be imported uniquely.
If some visible definitions of a group are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.
The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

The effect of importing a group is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions (including sub-groups) of this group except of those that are listed in the except specification.
See also clause 8.2.3.
Import statements contained in the group or in its subgroups are not part of this list, only definitions are.

It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) The group to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported.
b) See the restrictions given in clause 8.2.3.
The all keyword may be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.
The all keyword used with the constant keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the definitions part of the module the import statement refers to.

Similarly the all keyword used with the function keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions defined and the visible module control function in the module the import statement denotes.
If some visible declarations of a kind are wished to be excluded from the given import statement, their identifiers shall be listed following the except keyword.

The import of visible definitions of the same kind can be used in combination with imports of single visible definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type all [ except { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( template all [ except { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( const all [ except { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( testcase all [ except { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( altstep all [ except { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( function all [ except { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( signature all [ except { SignatureIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( modulepar all [ except { ModuleParIdentifier [ "," ] } ] )
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]
The effect of importing definitions of the same kind is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification.
See also clause 8.2.3.
NOTE: If the list of all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.
This case does not lead to an error.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) See the restrictions given in clause 8.2.3.

import from MyModule { type all; // imports all types of MyModule template all // imports all templates of MyModule } import from MyModule { type all except MyType3, MyType5; // imports all types except MyType3 and MyType5 template all // imports all templates defined in Mymodule }
All visible definitions of a module definitions part may be imported using the all keyword next to the module name.
If some visible definitions are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.
The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all visible declarations of the same kind from the import statement.
NOTE 1: If the list of all visible definitions of a module except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.
This case does not lead to an error.

NOTE 2: Importing all definitions of a module imports only definitions declared directly in that module including the address type and module control function (if they are specified), but does not import the import statements of that module (see also clause 8.2.3.7).

[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId
     all
     [ 
       {
          except "{"
            ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) 
          "}" 
          [ ";" ] 
       }
     ]
  [ ";" ]

The effect of importing all visible definitions of a module is identical to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except of those that are listed in the except specification.
See also clause 8.2.3.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:

a) If all visible definitions of a module are imported by using the all keyword, no other form of import (import of single definitions, import of the same kind, etc.) shall be used for the same import statement.

TTCN-3 supports the referencing of elements defined in other TTCN-3 editions (versioned elements) or other languages (foreign elements) from within TTCN-3 modules.
Such elements can be used in a TTCN-3 module of a given edition only if they have a TTCN-3 view in that TTCN-3 edition.

The term TTCN-3 view can be best explained by considering the case when the definition of a TTCN-3 element is based on another TTCN-3 element, the information content of the referenced element shall be available and is used for the new definition.
For example, when a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of fields of the core type shall be accessible and are used for the template definition.
In a similar way, when a core type is a versioned or foreign element it shall provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.
The versioned or foreign element, naturally, may contain more information than required by TTCN-3.
The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element means that part of the information carried by that element, which is necessary to use it in TTCN-3.
Obviously, the TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element may be the full set or a subset of the information content of that element but never a superset.
There may be versioned or foreign element without a TTCN-3 view (zero TTCN-3 view), i.e. for some reason no TTCN-3 definition in the given edition could be based on them.
To make declarations of versioned or foreign element visible in TTCN-3 modules, their names shall be imported just like definitions in other TTCN-3 modules of the given edition.
When imported, only the TTCN-3 view of the versioned or foreign element will be seen from the importing TTCN-3 module.
There are two main differences between importing TTCN-3 elements of the same editions and versioned or foreign elements:
To import from a TTCN-3 module of another edition or from a non-TTCN-3 module, the import statement shall contain an appropriate language identifier string.
Only versioned or foreign elements with a TTCN-3 view of a given edition are importable into a TTCN-3 module of that edition.

Importing can be done automatically using the all directive, in which case all importable objects shall automatically be selected by the testing tool, or done manually by listing names of elements to be imported.
Naturally, in the second case only importable elements are allowed in the list.
When importing definitions from a non-TTCN-3 language, two principle approaches exist:

With an implicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions are mapped internally in the TTCN-3 tool to the respective TTCN-3 definitions as defined by the language mapping; the importing module works with the internal representations of the imported definitions.

With an explicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions are mapped directly to separate TTCN-3 definitions; the importing module imports the generated TTCN-3 and works with the mapped TTCN-3 definitions.
These lead to three options when using non-TTCN-3 language modules in a TTCN-3 specification:

The import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool uses the internal representation of the implicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

The import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool imports from a TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

The import statement imports the explicit TTCN-3 representation of the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool imports the TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module according to the language mapping specification of that language.
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:
a) The language specification should only be omitted if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and the TTCN-3 version is known.

NOTE: The import mechanism is designed to allow the re-use of definitions from other TTCN-3 editions or from other non-TTCN-3 language sources.

TTCN-3 supports importing of visible import statements from other TTCN-3 modules.
This means that import statements of the module, from which the import statements are imported, are re-imported to the importing module.

For example, if module B imports the import statements of module A, everything that is imported by A using import statements visible for module B, is also imported by B. If another module C imports all import statements from B, then C imports all what A is importing - provided that the import statements are visible to modules B and C.
It is not possible to import individual import statements of another module.

The import of import statements can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), and with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4).
In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:

Friendship to modules is defined by the exporting module (the module that declares the definitions) not by the importing module (the module that uses the module definitions of another module).

If a module is friend to a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with public and friend visibility are visible to the friend module.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: A module definition SHALL be evaluated at the latest before the first reference to it.
requirements.original: A definition shall be evaluated latest before the first reference to it.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: A module definition that is not used NEED NOT be evaluated at all.
requirements.original: NOTE: If a definition is not used, it may not be evaluated at all.

readings: A module definition that is not used NEED NOT be evaluated.
A module definition that is not used SHALL NOT be evaluated.
ambiguity.issue: 'may not be evaluated' can be read as a possibility or as a prohibition; the possibility reading is chosen as it fits the preceding rule.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition outside of other scope units IS globally visible within the module.
requirements.original: Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition MAY be used elsewhere in the module.
requirements.original: They may be used elsewhere in the module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An identifier imported from another module IS globally visible within the importing module and MAY be used elsewhere in it.
requirements.original: This includes identifiers imported from other modules. Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A declaration of a dynamic language element, such as a variable or a timer, SHALL only be made in a test case, function, altstep or component type.
requirements.original: Declarations of dynamic language elements such as variables or timers shall only be made in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types.

readings: Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types (list is exhaustive).
Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps, component types and the module control part.
ambiguity.issue: The list omits the module control part, in which variables and timers are allowed (clause 26); the literal list is kept in the canonical text, the control part is considered allowed by clause 26.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definitions-part
requirements.canonical: A variable SHALL NOT be declared in the module definitions part (TTCN-3 has no global variables).
requirements.original: TTCN-3 does not support the declaration of variables in the module definitions part, i.e. global variables cannot be defined in TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:component-variable
requirements.canonical: A component variable MAY be used by all test cases, functions and altsteps running on a component of that component type.
requirements.original: However, variables defined in a test component type may be used by all test cases, functions, etc. running on components of that component type.

improper_terms.used: variables defined in a test component type

ambiguity.issue: Glossary term 'component variable' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter IS a value or template that MAY be supplied by the test system at runtime.
requirements.original: Module parameters are values or templates that may be supplied by the test environment at runtime.

ambiguity.issue: The glossary term is 'test system'.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter IS NOT changed during test execution.
requirements.original: Module parameters do not change during test execution.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter MAY be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters and in template definitions.
requirements.original: They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be used within a type definition.
requirements.original: They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter declaration has the syntax [Visibility] `modulepar` [TemplateModifier] [TypeOrNestedTypeDef] Identifier [":=" TemplateBody] {"," Identifier [":=" TemplateBody]} ";".
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] modulepar [ TemplateModifier ]
     [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ]
     { Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] "," }
     Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] ";"

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter behaves at runtime as a global constant or as an unparameterized template.
requirements.original: Module parameters behave as global constants or unparameterized templates at runtime.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: Module parameterization IS restricted to value parameterization.
requirements.original: For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.

readings: Module parameters are only supported as static (value) parameterization resolved at start of runtime, which includes template module parameters.
Module parameters SHALL only be values, not templates.
ambiguity.issue: 'value parameterization' conflicts with template module parameters allowed by s001/s004; the reading 'static parameterization (values and templates) resolved at start of runtime' is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual values of module parameters SHALL be resolved statically at the start of runtime.
requirements.original: For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: Module parameters allow a TTCN-3 test suite to be customized for a specific IUT, test setup or test campaign.
requirements.original: Module parameters allow to customize a TTCN-3 test suite for a specific IUT, test setup or test campaign.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter declaration MAY specify a default value or template for the module parameter.
requirements.original: It is allowed to specify a default value or template for each module parameter as part of the modulepar declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: the test system does not provide a value or template for the module parameter
requirements.canonical: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the default value or template given in the declaration SHALL be used during test execution.
requirements.original: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: the test system provides a value or template for the module parameter
requirements.canonical: If the test system provides an actual value or template for a module parameter, that actual value or template SHALL be used during test execution instead of the default.
requirements.original: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of a module parameter IS either given explicitly or determined implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing.
requirements.original: The type of the module parameter is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: automatic typing is used
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the declaration IS omitted.
requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block and restriction i) use 'TypeOrNestedTypeDef'.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: automatic typing is used
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the type of the module parameter IS the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: functions are used in the initialization of a module parameter
requirements.canonical: If functions are used for the initialization of a module parameter, they SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: If functions are used for the initialization of module parameters, it is strongly advised to adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: Initializing a module parameter with functions that do not follow the rules of clause 16.1.4 CAN cause non-deterministic test executions.
requirements.original: Not following these rules may cause non-deterministic test executions. If functions are used for the initialization of module parameters, it is strongly advised to adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A visible module parameter MAY be imported.
requirements.original: Visible module parameters can be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record or set module parameter or module parameter field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
requirements.original: Optional fields of record and set module parameters or module parameter fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: the optional fields are to be initialized implicitly
requirements.canonical: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or module parameter field, an `optional` attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with it, either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
requirements.original: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or a module parameter field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as the target of an assignment.
requirements.original: a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as an actual `out` or `inout` parameter.
requirements.original: a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be of port, default, timer or component type.
requirements.original: b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
requirements.original: b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL only be of the address type if the address type is explicitly defined within the module containing the module parameter declaration.
requirements.original: c) A module parameter shall only be of type address if the address type is explicitly defined within the associated module.

readings: The address type SHALL be defined in the module that declares the module parameter.
The address type SHALL be defined in, or be visible (e.g. imported) in, the module associated with the module parameter.
ambiguity.issue: 'explicitly defined within the associated module' does not say whether an imported address type definition suffices; the literal reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be declared only within the module definitions part.
requirements.original: d) Module parameters shall be declared within the module definition part only.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 8.2 uses the name 'module definitions part'.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module MAY contain more than one module parameter declaration.
requirements.original: e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be declared only once, i.e. a module parameter SHALL NOT be redefined.
requirements.original: e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration.
requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL conform to the TemplateModifier of the declaration.
requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.subject: ent:template-body
requirements.condition: no TemplateModifier is present
requirements.canonical: If no TemplateModifier is present in a module parameter declaration, the TemplateBody SHALL resolve to a value.
requirements.original: If no TemplateModifier is present, the TemplateBody shall resolve to a value. f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be used in a type definition or array definition.
requirements.original: g) Module parameters shall not be used in type or array definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: Every sub-element of component or default type of the default value of a module parameter SHALL be initialized with the special value `null`.
requirements.original: h) All sub-elements of component or default type of a default value of a module parameter shall be initialized with the special value null.

readings: Sub-elements of component or default type in the default value SHALL be `null`.
This rule implies that module parameters of structured types with component or default sub-elements are allowed, which restriction b) does not forbid; only the default must use `null`.
ambiguity.issue: Restriction b) forbids top-level component and default types but only forbids port/timer sub-elements; the first reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a module parameter declaration, the assignment part ":=" TemplateBody SHALL be present.
requirements.original: i) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: Definitions in the module definitions part MAY be collected in named groups.
requirements.original: In the module definitions part, definitions can be collected in named groups.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: Grouping of definitions IS done to aid readability and to add logical structure to the module.
requirements.original: Grouping is done to aid readability and to add logical structure to the module if required.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.condition: a sub-group needs to be identified uniquely
requirements.canonical: If necessary to identify a sub-group uniquely within the group hierarchy (e.g. for the import of a specific sub-group), the dot notation SHALL be used.
requirements.original: If necessary, the dot notation shall be used to identify sub-groups within the group hierarchy uniquely, e.g. for the import of a specific sub-group.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group definition has the syntax [`public`] `group` GroupIdentifier "{" {ModuleDefinition [";"]} "}".

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group of definitions MAY be specified wherever a single module definition is allowed.
requirements.original: A group of definitions can be specified wherever a single definition is allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group MAY contain other groups (groups MAY be nested).
requirements.original: Groups may be nested, i.e. groups may contain other groups.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group or nested group IS NOT a scope unit (groups have no scoping).
requirements.original: Groups and nested groups have no scoping.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: Attributes given to a group by an associated `with` statement apply to all elements of the group.
requirements.original: However, attributes given to a group by an associated with statement apply to all elements of a group (see clause 27).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY import a group, so that all visible elements of the group are imported.
requirements.original: Import statements may import groups so that all visible elements of a group are imported (see clause 8.2.3.3).

requirements.subject: ent:group-identifier
requirements.canonical: Group identifiers NEED NOT be unique across the whole module.
requirements.original: a) Group identifiers across the whole module need not necessarily be unique.

requirements.subject: ent:group-identifier
requirements.canonical: Top-level group identifiers of a module SHALL be unique.
requirements.original: However, top-level group identifiers and all group identifiers of subgroups of a single group shall be unique.

readings: Top-level group identifiers SHALL be unique among the top-level groups of the module.
Top-level group identifiers SHALL be unique among all top-level identifiers of the module.
ambiguity.issue: It is not stated against which set of identifiers uniqueness is required; the first reading is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:group-identifier
requirements.canonical: The group identifiers of the direct sub-groups of a single group SHALL be unique.
requirements.original: However, top-level group identifiers and all group identifiers of subgroups of a single group shall be unique.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: Only public visibility SHALL be defined for a group (a group SHALL NOT be declared `private` or `friend`).
requirements.original: b) Only public visibility can be defined for groups as they are always public.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group IS always public.
requirements.original: b) Only public visibility can be defined for groups as they are always public.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Visible definitions specified in a different module MAY be re-used by means of the import statement.
requirements.original: It is possible to re-use visible definitions specified in different modules using the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: Every definition in a TTCN-3 module has an associated visibility.
requirements.original: Every definition in a TTCN-3 module has an associated visibility, which is by default public (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: The default visibility of a definition in a TTCN-3 module IS public.
requirements.original: Every definition in a TTCN-3 module has an associated visibility, which is by default public (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group IS public only.
requirements.original: NOTE: Groups are public only.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing a group imports only the visible elements of the group.
requirements.original: Importing a group means that only the visible elements of the group are being imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY be used anywhere in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: An import statement can be used anywhere in the module definitions part.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement has the syntax [Visibility] `import from` ModuleId [-> LocalModuleName] followed by either `all` [`except` "{" ExceptSpec "}"] or "{" ImportSpec "}", optionally terminated by ";".
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId [-> LocalModuleName]
     ( 
       ( all [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] ) 
       |
       ( "{" ImportSpec "}" )
     )
  [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY import module parameters, user-defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and testcases.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the import of the following definitions: module parameters, user defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and test cases.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses "test cases" for the TTCN-3 testcase definitions and "user defined types" without hyphen.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An importable definition IS composed of a name (its identifier), a specification and, for functions, altsteps and testcases, an associated behaviour description.
requirements.original: Each definition has a name (defines the identifier of the definition, e.g. a function name), a specification (e.g. a type specification or a signature of a function) and in the case of functions, altsteps and test cases an associated behaviour description.

ambiguity.issue: "test cases" is used for TTCN-3 testcase definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement of a module MAY be explicitly imported by another module.
requirements.original: In addition, import statements of one module can be explicitly imported by another module (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition or an import statement that is not visible from the importing module.
requirements.original: Only definitions or import statements visible from the importing module can be imported (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.canonical: A module definition IS public by default.
requirements.original: In contrast to module definitions, which are by default public, import statements are by default private.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement IS private by default.
requirements.original: In contrast to module definitions, which are by default public, import statements are by default private.

requirements.subject: ent:behaviour-description
requirements.canonical: The behaviour description of an imported function, altstep or testcase IS NOT visible to the importer and has no effect on the import mechanism.
requirements.original: Behaviour descriptions have no effect on the import mechanism, because their internals are considered to be invisible to the importer when the corresponding functions, altsteps or test cases are imported.

requirements.subject: ent:specification-part
requirements.canonical: The specification part of an importable definition IS composed of local definitions (e.g. field names, enumerated values) and referenced definitions (e.g. references to types, templates, constants or module parameters).
requirements.original: The specification part of an importable definition contains local definitions (e.g. field names of structured type definitions or values of enumerated types) and referenced definitions (e.g. references to type definitions, templates, constants or module parameters).

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition IS an identifier that is newly defined in the importable definition.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The local definitions column refers to identifiers only that are newly defined in the importable definition.

requirements.subject: ent:field-name
requirements.canonical: A field name used in a template definition IS a referenced definition that is referenced via the type of the template.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The referenced definitions field1, field2 and field3 of template MyTemplate are the field names of MyType5, i.e. they are referenced via MyType5.

ambiguity.issue: The note names the template "MyTemplate" while the example defines "m_myTemplate".

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-definition
requirements.canonical: A referenced definition IS itself an importable definition consisting of a name and a specification part with local and referenced definitions.
requirements.original: Referenced definitions are also importable definitions, i.e. the source of a referenced definition can again be structured into a name and a specification part and the specification part also contains local and referenced definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An importable definition CAN be built up recursively from other importable definitions.
requirements.original: In other words, an importable definition may be built up recursively from other importable definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported module parameter ARE the module parameter type.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Module parameter; Possible Referenced Definitions: Module parameter type

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported enumerated type ARE its enumerated values.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • enumerated type; Possible Local Definitions: Concrete values

ambiguity.issue: Table 8 calls the enumerated values of an enumerated type "concrete values".

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported structured type ARE its field names and nested type definitions.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • structured type; Possible Local Definitions: Field names, nested type definitions; Possible Referenced Definitions: Field types

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported structured type ARE its field types.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • structured type; Possible Local Definitions: Field names, nested type definitions; Possible Referenced Definitions: Field types

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported port type ARE its message types and signatures.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • port type; Possible Referenced Definitions: Message types, signatures

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported component type ARE its constant names, variable names, timer names and port names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • component type; Possible Local Definitions: Constant names, variable names, timer names and port names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Constant types, variable types, port types

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported component type ARE its constant types, variable types and port types.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: • component type; Possible Local Definitions: Constant names, variable names, timer names and port names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Constant types, variable types, port types

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported signature ARE its parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Signature; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type, types of exceptions

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported signature ARE its parameter types, return type and exception types.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Signature; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type, types of exceptions

requirements.subject: ent:constant
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported constant ARE the constant type.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Constant; Possible Referenced Definitions: Constant type

requirements.subject: ent:data-template
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported data template ARE its formal parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Data Template; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Template type, parameter types, constants, module parameters, functions

requirements.subject: ent:data-template
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported data template ARE its template type, formal parameter types, constants, module parameters and functions.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Data Template; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Template type, parameter types, constants, module parameters, functions

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported signature template ARE its signature definition, constants, module parameters and functions.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Signature template; Possible Referenced Definitions: Signature definition, constants, module parameters functions

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported function ARE its formal parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Function; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type, component type (runs on clause)

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported function ARE its formal parameter types, return type and the component type of its `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Function; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type, component type (runs on clause)

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported external function ARE its formal parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: External function; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type

requirements.subject: ent:external-function
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported external function ARE its formal parameter types and return type.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: External function; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, return type

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported altstep ARE its formal parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Altstep; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component type (runs on clause)

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported altstep ARE its formal parameter types and the component type of its `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Altstep; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component type (runs on clause)

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter names.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Test case; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component types (runs on- and system clause)

ambiguity.issue: Table 8 uses "Test case" for the TTCN-3 testcase definition.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter types and the component types of its `runs on` and `system` clauses.
requirements.original: Importable Definition: Test case; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component types (runs on- and system clause)

ambiguity.issue: Table 8 uses "Test case" for the TTCN-3 testcase definition.

requirements.subject: ent:import-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The import mechanism distinguishes between the identifier of a referenced definition and the information necessary for the usage of the referenced definition within the imported definition.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 import mechanism distinguishes between the identifier of a referenced definition and the information _necessary for the usage of a referenced definition within the imported definition.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-definition
requirements.canonical: The identifier of a referenced definition IS NOT imported automatically when the definition referencing it is imported.
requirements.original: For the usage, the identifier of a_ referenced definition is not required and therefore not imported automatically.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: the imported definition has attributes defined by means of a with statement
requirements.canonical: If an imported definition has attributes defined by a `with` statement, the attributes SHALL also be imported.
requirements.original: If an imported definition has attributes (defined by means of a with statement) then the attributes shall also be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: A global attribute of a module IS associated with each definition of the module that does not have this attribute itself.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: If the module has global attributes they are associated to definitions without these attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL resolve situations where the same definition is referred to more than once by import statements.
requirements.original: Such cases shall be resolved by the system and definitions shall be imported only once.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.condition: the same definition is referred to more than once by imports
requirements.canonical: A definition referred to more than once by import statements (single definitions, groups, definitions of the same kind) SHALL be imported only once.
requirements.original: Such cases shall be resolved by the system and definitions shall be imported only once.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHOULD provide mechanisms (e.g. overwriting, warnings to the user) to resolve multiple imports of the same definition.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: The mechanisms to resolve such ambiguities, e.g. overwriting and sending warnings to the user, are outside the scope of the present document and should be provided by TTCN-3 tools.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import statements and the definitions within import statements ARE treated independently one after the other in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: All import statements and definitions within import statements are considered to be treated independently one after the other in the order of their appearance.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module SHALL have its own name space.
requirements.original: All TTCN-3 modules shall have their own name space in which all definitions shall be uniquely identified.

requirements.subject: ent:name-space
requirements.canonical: Each definition in the name space of a module SHALL be uniquely identified.
requirements.original: All TTCN-3 modules shall have their own name space in which all definitions shall be uniquely identified.

requirements.subject: ent:name-clash
requirements.canonical: A name clash CAN occur due to import, e.g. import from different modules.
requirements.original: Name _clashes may occur due to import, e.g. import from different modules.

requirements.subject: ent:name-clash
requirements.canonical: A name clash caused by an imported definition SHALL be resolved by using the qualified name, i.e. prefixing the imported definition with the identifier of the module in which it is defined.
requirements.original: Name clashes shall be resolved using qualified_ name(s) for the imported definition(s), i.e. prefixing the imported definition (which causes the name clash) by the identifier of the module in which it has been defined; the prefix and the identifier shall be separated by a dot (".").

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.canonical: In a qualified name the module identifier prefix and the definition identifier SHALL be separated by a dot (".").
requirements.original: Name clashes shall be resolved using qualified_ name(s) for the imported definition(s), i.e. prefixing the imported definition (which causes the name clash) by the identifier of the module in which it has been defined; the prefix and the identifier shall be separated by a dot (".").

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.condition: the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known
requirements.canonical: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (component reference is a variable, a value returned from a function, or the type is given in the `runs on`, `mtc` or `system` clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in this component type.
requirements.original: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is about connection operations and does not belong to the import clause; it seems to have been copied here by mistake and it separates the name-clash rule from the "one exception to this rule" that follows. Chose the literal reading as a general rule for connection operations.
readings: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known, the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in this component type.
If the type of an imported component referenced in a connection operation is known, the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in that imported component type.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.condition: in the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashes with the name of a definition in the importing module
requirements.canonical: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value that clashes with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence over that definition.
requirements.original: There is one exception to this rule: when in the context of an enumerated type (see clause 6.2.4), an enumerated value is clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module, the enumerated value shall take precedence and the definition in the importing module shall be referenced by using its qualified name (see example 5 below in this clause).

ambiguity.issue: "this rule" can refer to the directly preceding sentence (port declarations in connection operations) or to the name-clash resolution rule before it; the content shows that the name-clash rule is meant.
readings: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the rule that name clashes are resolved by prefixing the imported definition.

In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the port declaration rule for connection operations.

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.condition: in the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashes with the name of a definition in the importing module
requirements.canonical: In the context of an enumerated type, a definition of the importing module whose name clashes with an enumerated value SHALL be referenced by its qualified name.
requirements.original: There is one exception to this rule: when in the context of an enumerated type (see clause 6.2.4), an enumerated value is clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module, the enumerated value shall take precedence and the definition in the importing module shall be referenced by using its qualified name (see example 5 below in this clause).
