ambiguity.issue: "this rule" can refer to the directly preceding sentence (port declarations in connection operations) or to the name-clash resolution rule before it; the content shows that the name-clash rule is meant.
readings: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the rule that name clashes are resolved by prefixing the imported definition.

In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the port declaration rule for connection operations.

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.condition: there are no ambiguities
requirements.canonical: If there is no ambiguity, an imported definition NEED NOT be prefixed with its module identifier when it is used.
requirements.original: In cases where there are no ambiguities the prefixing need not (but may) be present when the imported definitions are used.

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.condition: there are no ambiguities
requirements.canonical: If there is no ambiguity, an imported definition MAY be prefixed with its module identifier when it is used.
requirements.original: In cases where there are no ambiguities the prefixing need not (but may) be present when the imported definitions are used.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the definition is referenced in the module where it is defined
requirements.canonical: When a definition is referenced in the module where it is defined, the identifier of the current module MAY be used as prefix of the definition identifier.
requirements.original: When the definition is referenced in the same module where it is defined, the module identifier of the module (the current module) also may be used for prefixing the identifier of the definition.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the definition is referenced in the module where it is defined
requirements.canonical: Prefixing with the identifier of the current module SHALL only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.
requirements.original: For the latter case, prefixing shall only be used for definitions with global visibility for the module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY rename the imported module.
requirements.original: It is allowed to rename a module name during its import.

requirements.subject: ent:local-module-name
requirements.canonical: The new name given to a module renamed during import IS visible only in the importing module.
requirements.original: The new name will be visible only in the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL only be used in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

ambiguity.issue: "a function definition and alike" does not list the excluded constructs; the example also shows the control part. Chose all behaviour definitions and the control part.
readings: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function definition or any other definition outside the module definitions part (e.g. component types, groups' members are allowed).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL import only top-level definitions of a module that are visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: b) Only top-level visible definitions of a module may be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a top-level definition that is invisible to the importing module.
requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition that occurs at a lower scope than the module (e.g. a local constant defined in a function).
requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with its name and all its local definitions.
requirements.original: c) A definition is imported together with its name and all local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition (e.g. a field name of a record type or an enumerated value) has meaning only in the context of the definition in which it is defined; e.g. a field name of a record type IS usable only to access a field of that record type.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: A local definition, e.g. a field name of a user-defined record type or an enumerated value, has only meaning in the context of the definitions in which it is defined, e.g. a field name of a record type can only be used to access a field of the record type and not outside this context.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: Importing an enumerated type IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.original: In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 5 states that in module B (which imports enumerated type MyEnumType) the constant "const MyEnumType enumY" is not allowed because enumerated values restrict global names, which seems to contradict this sentence. Chose the literal text; the example may mean that the clash is only forbidden in the context of the enumerated type.
readings: Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type without restriction.

Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type, except where the definition is in the context of that enumerated type (then clause 6.2.4 applies).

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with all information of its referenced definitions that is necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions.
requirements.original: d) A definition is imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.condition: module C imports from module B a definition that references a type defined in module A
requirements.canonical: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type defined in module A, the information necessary for the usage of that type IS automatically imported into module C.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type reference defined in module A, the corresponding information necessary for the usage of that type is automatically imported into module C (see example 6 below in this clause).

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.condition: module C imports value, template or local definitions of an enumerated type from module B
requirements.canonical: If module C imports from module B global value or template definitions (constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (formal parameters, component constants and variables) of an enumerated type, the enumerated values of that type ARE implicitly imported into module C and are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C.
requirements.original: In particular, if module C imports global value or template definitions (e.g. constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (e.g. formal parameters of templates, functions, etc. or constants and variables of component types) of an enumerated type from module B, the enumerated values of this type (i.e. the identifiers) are implicitly and automatically imported to module C. That is, the enumerated values are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C (e.g. when an actual parameter is passed or a value is assigned to a component variable).

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: The implicit import of enumerated values IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.original: Note that this implicit importing does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in module C.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-definition
requirements.condition: the referenced definition is to be used in the importing module
requirements.canonical: A referenced definition that is to be used in the importing module SHALL be explicitly imported, either directly from its source module or by importing the import statements of a module that imports it.
requirements.original: e) If the referenced definitions are wished to be used in the importing module, they shall be explicitly imported either directly from its source module or indirectly by importing the import statements of a module importing it (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:behaviour-description
requirements.canonical: When a function, altstep or testcase is imported, its behaviour specification and all definitions used inside it ARE NOT visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: "test case" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; "behaviour specification" is used where the semantic description says "behaviour description".

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import statement SHALL NOT override the language specification of the importing module.
requirements.original: g) The language specification (see clause 8.1) of the import statement shall not override the language specification of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: a language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.canonical: If the source module defines a language specification, the language specification of an import statement importing from it SHALL be identical to the language specification of the source module.
requirements.original: h) The language specification of the import statement shall be identical to the language specification of the source module from which definitions are imported (see clause 8.2.3.8) provided a language specification is defined in the source module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: no language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.canonical: If the source module does not define a language specification, the language specification of the import statement IS taken as the language specification of the source module.
requirements.original: If not, the language specification in the import statement is taken as the language specification of the source module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification given in the import statement
requirements.canonical: If the source module uses language concepts that are not part of the language specification taken from the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.

ambiguity.issue: "that language specification" most likely refers to the language specification taken from the import statement when the source module has none (previous sentence); it could also refer to any language specification of the import statement.
readings: If the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.

If the source module uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error, whether or not the source module defines a language specification.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name IS NOT imported.
requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name SHALL NOT be used for referencing the imported module.
requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.subject: ent:local-module-name
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: A module renamed in the import clause SHALL be referenced using its new local name only.
requirements.original: The imported module can be referenced using the new local name only.

requirements.subject: ent:local-module-name
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module SHALL be unique in the scope of the importing module.
requirements.original: j) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module shall be unique in the scope of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules ARE different definitions, even if their actual definitions are identical.
requirements.original: NOTE 7: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules are always assumed to be different, even if the actual definitions in the different modules are identical.

requirements.subject: ent:type
requirements.canonical: Importing a type that has the same name as a locally defined type results in two different types being available in the importing module.
requirements.original: For example, importing a type that is already defined locally, even with the same name, would lead to two different types being available in the module.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A visible single definition MAY be imported by referring to its definition kind and its definition name(s).
requirements.original: Single visible definitions can be imported by referring to the definition kind and the definition name(s).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of single definitions MAY be combined with imports of groups, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of single definitions can be used in combination with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for single definitions has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( type {TypeDefIdentifier [","]} | template {TemplateIdentifier [","]} | const {ConstIdentifier [","]} | testcase {TestcaseIdentifier [","]} | altstep {AltstepIdentifier [","]} | function {FunctionIdentifier [","]} | signature {SignatureIdentifier [","]} | modulepar {ModuleParIdentifier [","]} ) [";"] } "}" [";"].
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) | 
          ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } ) 
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports a definition which is not visible to the importing module SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Import of an invisible definition shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: A single definition to be imported SHALL be visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: a) The definition to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported and shall be visible to the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group of definitions MAY be imported.
requirements.original: Groups of definitions may be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of groups MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of definitions of the same kind and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of groups can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:sub-group
requirements.canonical: A sub-group MAY be imported directly, without importing the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.
requirements.original: It is allowed to import sub-groups (i.e. a group which is defined within another group) directly, i.e. without the groups in which the sub-group is embedded.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the name of the sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module
requirements.canonical: If the name of a sub-group to be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module, the import statement SHALL use the dot notation to identify the sub-group uniquely.
requirements.original: If the name of a sub-group that should be imported is identical to the name of another sub-group in the same module (see clause 8.2.2), the dot notation shall be used to identify the sub-group to be imported uniquely.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible definitions of the group are not to be imported
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions of an imported group are not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible definitions of a group are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of a group import.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of a group import excludes all definitions of that kind of the group from the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all definitions of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for groups has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ except "{" ExceptSpec "}" ] [","] } ) [";"] } "}" [";"].

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing a group IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of the group, including its sub-groups, except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing a group is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions (including sub-groups) of this group except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import statements contained in an imported group or in its sub-groups ARE NOT part of the group import; only definitions are imported.
requirements.original: Import statements contained in the group or in its subgroups are not part of this list, only definitions are.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: An except specification of an import statement IS NOT an exclusion of the listed definitions from being imported by other imports.
requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of the same kind IS a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
requirements.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: An except specification excludes definitions only from the single list of definitions of the import to which it belongs.
requirements.original: The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group to be imported SHALL be defined in the module from which it is imported.
requirements.original: a) The group to be imported shall be defined in the module from which it is to be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.
requirements.original: The all keyword may be used to import all visible definitions of the same kind of a module.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used with the `const` keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the module definitions part of the module referenced by the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword used with the constant keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the definitions part of the module the import statement refers to.

ambiguity.issue: 'constant keyword' is used, the TTCN-3 keyword is `const`.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used with the `function` keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions and the visible module control part of the module referenced by the import statement.
requirements.original: Similarly the all keyword used with the function keyword identifies all visible functions, all visible external functions defined and the visible module control function in the module the import statement denotes.

ambiguity.issue: 'module control function' is used for the module control part, which is not a function elsewhere in the standard.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible declarations of the kind are to be excluded
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions of a kind are to be excluded from an import of all definitions of that kind, their identifiers SHALL be listed following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible declarations of a kind are wished to be excluded from the given import statement, their identifiers shall be listed following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of groups and imports of import statements.
requirements.original: The import of visible definitions of the same kind can be used in combination with imports of single visible definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), and with imports of import statements (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for definitions of the same kind has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId "{" { ( Kind all [ except { Identifier [","] } ] ) [";"] } "}" [";"], where Kind is one of type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId "{" 
     {
       (
          ( type all [ except { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( template all [ except { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( const all [ except { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( testcase all [ except { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( altstep all [ except { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( function all [ except { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( signature all [ except { SignatureIdentifier [ "," ] } ] ) |
          ( modulepar all [ except { ModuleParIdentifier [ "," ] } ] )
       ) 
       [ ";" ] 
     }
  "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing definitions of the same kind IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing definitions of the same kind is identical to an import statement that lists all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the resulting list of definitions is empty
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
requirements.original: NOTE: If the list of all visible definitions of that kind except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of definitions of the same kind whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
requirements.original: This case does not lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY import all visible definitions of the module definitions part of a module by using the `all` keyword next to the module name.
requirements.original: All visible definitions of a module definitions part may be imported using the all keyword next to the module name.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.condition: some visible definitions are not to be imported
requirements.canonical: If visible definitions are not to be imported by an import of all definitions of a module, their kinds and identifiers SHALL be listed in the exception list enclosed in curly brackets following the `except` keyword.
requirements.original: If some visible definitions are wished not to be imported, their kinds and identifiers shall be listed in the exception list within a pair of curly brackets following the except keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used in the exception list of an import of all definitions of a module.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all visible declarations of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:all-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword used for a definition kind in the exception list of an import of all definitions excludes all visible declarations of that kind from the import statement.
requirements.original: The all keyword is also allowed to be used in the exception list; this will exclude all visible declarations of the same kind from the import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the resulting list of definitions is empty
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of visible definitions, after removing the excepted ones, is empty has no effect.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: If the list of all visible definitions of a module except of those that are listed in the except specification is empty, the import statement has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module whose resulting list of definitions is empty DOES NOT cause an error.
requirements.original: This case does not lead to an error.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module imports only the definitions declared directly in that module, including the address type and the module control part if they are specified.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Importing all definitions of a module imports only definitions declared directly in that module including the address type and module control function (if they are specified), but does not import the import statements of that module (see also clause 8.2.3.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'module control function' is used for the module control part.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of all definitions of a module DOES NOT import the import statements of that module.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Importing all definitions of a module imports only definitions declared directly in that module including the address type and module control function (if they are specified), but does not import the import statements of that module (see also clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement for all definitions of a module has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleId all [ { except "{" ( Kind { Identifier [","] } | all ) ... "}" [";"] } ] [";"], where Kind is one of group, type, template, const, testcase, altstep, function, signature or modulepar.
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleId
     all
     [ 
       {
          except "{"
            ( group { QualifiedIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( type { TypeDefIdentifier [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( template { TemplateIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( const { ConstIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( testcase { TestcaseIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( altstep { AltstepIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( function { FunctionIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( signature { SignatureIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) | 
            ( modulepar { ModuleParIdentifier  [ "," ] } | all ) 
          "}" 
          [ ";" ] 
       }
     ]
  [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing all visible definitions of a module IS equivalent to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except those listed in the except specification.
requirements.original: The effect of importing all visible definitions of a module is identical to an import statement that lists all importable definitions of that module except of those that are listed in the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: all visible definitions of a module are imported with the `all` keyword
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports all visible definitions of a module with the `all` keyword SHALL NOT contain any other form of import (import of single definitions, import of definitions of the same kind, etc.).
requirements.original: a) If all visible definitions of a module are imported by using the all keyword, no other form of import (import of single definitions, import of the same kind, etc.) shall be used for the same import statement.

requirements.subject: ent:except-specification
requirements.canonical: The except specification of an import of all definitions SHALL contain at most one except entry per kind of definition (group, type, etc.).
requirements.original: b) In the set of except statements for an all import, only one except statement per kind of definition (i.e. for a group, type, etc.) is allowed.

ambiguity.issue: 'except statement' is used for the per-kind entries of the except specification.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: definitions are imported from another TTCN-3 edition or a non-TTCN-3 source
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports visible definitions from a module of another TTCN-3 edition or from a non-TTCN-3 source SHALL use the language specification to denote the language, optionally with a version number, of the source.
requirements.original: In cases when visible definitions are imported from modules from other TTCN-3 editions or from other sources than TTCN-3 modules, the language specification (see clause 8.1) shall be used to denote the language (may be together with a version number) of the source (e.g. module, package, library or even file) from which definitions are imported.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: A language specification consists of the `language` keyword followed by a textual declaration of the denoted language.
requirements.original: It consists of the language keyword and a subsequent textual declaration of the denoted language.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: the source module is a TTCN-3 module of the same edition as the importing module
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import statement MAY be omitted when importing from a TTCN-3 module of the same edition as the importing module.
requirements.original: The use of the language specification is optional when importing from a TTCN-3 module of the same edition as the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: A language specification denoting a TTCN-3 edition SHALL use the TTCN-3 language identifiers defined in clause 8.1.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 language identifiers defined in clause 8.1 are to be used.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: A language specification MAY additionally use the package identifiers defined in ETSI ES 202 781, ETSI ES 202 782, ETSI ES 202 784 and ETSI ES 202 785.
requirements.original: Package identifiers from ETSI ES 202 781 [i.11], ETSI ES 202 782 [i.14], ETSI ES 202 784 [i.12] and ETSI ES 202 785 [i.13] can be used in addition.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether package identifiers may be used instead of or only together with a TTCN-3 language identifier.
readings: A language specification MAY contain package identifiers in addition to a TTCN-3 language identifier.
A language specification MAY consist of package identifiers as an alternative to TTCN-3 language identifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: an incompatibility between language identification and module syntax is discovered
requirements.canonical: When an incompatibility is discovered between the language or package identification (including implicit identification by omitting the language specification) and the syntax of the module from which definitions are imported, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL make a reasonable effort to resolve the conflict.
requirements.original: When an incompatibility is discovered between the language and/or package identification (including implicit identification by omitting the language specification) and the syntax of the module from which definitions are imported, tools shall provide reasonable effort to resolve the conflict.

ambiguity.issue: 'Reasonable effort' is not defined; it is unclear whether the tool must still report an error if resolution fails.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL attempt to resolve the conflict and MAY report an error if the attempt fails.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL resolve the conflict and SHALL NOT report an error.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleIdentifier [LanguageSpec] ... [";"], where the optional language specification follows the module identifier.
requirements.original: [ Visibility ] import from ModuleIdentifier [ LanguageSpec ] … [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned element IS an element defined in another TTCN-3 edition that is referenced from within a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the referencing of elements defined in other TTCN-3 editions (versioned elements) or other languages (foreign elements) from within TTCN-3 modules.

requirements.subject: ent:foreign-element
requirements.canonical: A foreign element IS an element defined in a language other than TTCN-3 that is referenced from within a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the referencing of elements defined in other TTCN-3 editions (versioned elements) or other languages (foreign elements) from within TTCN-3 modules.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned or foreign element SHALL NOT be used in a TTCN-3 module of a given edition unless it has a TTCN-3 view in that edition.
requirements.original: Such elements can be used in a TTCN-3 module of a given edition only if they have a TTCN-3 view in that TTCN-3 edition.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.canonical: When the definition of a TTCN-3 element is based on another TTCN-3 element, the information content of the referenced element SHALL be available and IS used for the new definition.
requirements.original: The term TTCN-3 view can be best explained by considering the case when the definition of a TTCN-3 element is based on another TTCN-3 element, the information content of the referenced element shall be available and is used for the new definition.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: When a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of the fields of that type SHALL be accessible and are used for the template definition.
requirements.original: For example, when a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of fields of the core type shall be accessible and are used for the template definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'core type' is used for the type on which the template is based; the glossary defines core type as the type directly referencing the root type.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned or foreign element used as the type of a TTCN-3 definition SHALL provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.
requirements.original: In a similar way, when a core type is a versioned or foreign element it shall provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.

ambiguity.issue: 'core type' is used for the referenced type of a definition rather than in the glossary sense.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned or foreign element CAN contain more information than required by TTCN-3.
requirements.original: The versioned or foreign element, naturally, may contain more information than required by TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-view
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element IS that part of the information carried by the element which is necessary to use it in TTCN-3.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element means that part of the information carried by that element, which is necessary to use it in TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-view
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element IS the full set or a subset of the information content of that element and IS NOT a superset of it.
requirements.original: Obviously, the TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element may be the full set or a subset of the information content of that element but never a superset.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned or foreign element CAN have no TTCN-3 view, so that no TTCN-3 definition in the given edition can be based on it.
requirements.original: There may be versioned or foreign element without a TTCN-3 view (zero TTCN-3 view), i.e. for some reason no TTCN-3 definition in the given edition could be based on them.

requirements.subject: ent:zero-ttcn3-view
requirements.canonical: A zero TTCN-3 view IS the absence of a TTCN-3 view of a versioned or foreign element in a given edition.
requirements.original: There may be versioned or foreign element without a TTCN-3 view (zero TTCN-3 view), i.e. for some reason no TTCN-3 definition in the given edition could be based on them.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: The names of versioned or foreign element declarations SHALL be imported, like definitions of other TTCN-3 modules of the given edition, to make them visible in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: To make declarations of versioned or foreign element visible in TTCN-3 modules, their names shall be imported just like definitions in other TTCN-3 modules of the given edition.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: When a versioned or foreign element is imported, only its TTCN-3 view IS seen from the importing TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: When imported, only the TTCN-3 view of the versioned or foreign element will be seen from the importing TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the source is a TTCN-3 module of another edition or a non-TTCN-3 module
requirements.canonical: An import statement that imports from a TTCN-3 module of another edition or from a non-TTCN-3 module SHALL contain an appropriate language identifier string.
requirements.original: To import from a TTCN-3 module of another edition or from a non-TTCN-3 module, the import statement shall contain an appropriate language identifier string.

requirements.subject: ent:versioned-element
requirements.canonical: A versioned or foreign element without a TTCN-3 view of a given edition SHALL NOT be imported into a TTCN-3 module of that edition.
requirements.original: Only versioned or foreign elements with a TTCN-3 view of a given edition are importable into a TTCN-3 module of that edition.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: When importing is done with the `all` directive, the TTCN-3 tool SHALL automatically select all importable objects.
requirements.original: Importing can be done automatically using the all directive, in which case all importable objects shall automatically be selected by the testing tool, or done manually by listing names of elements to be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement MAY import elements by listing the names of the elements to be imported.
requirements.original: Importing can be done automatically using the all directive, in which case all importable objects shall automatically be selected by the testing tool, or done manually by listing names of elements to be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement that lists the names of elements to be imported SHALL list only importable elements.
requirements.original: Naturally, in the second case only importable elements are allowed in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-language-mapping
requirements.canonical: With an implicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions ARE mapped internally in the TTCN-3 tool to TTCN-3 definitions as defined by the language mapping, and the importing module works with the internal representations of the imported definitions.
requirements.original: With an implicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions are mapped internally in the TTCN-3 tool to the respective TTCN-3 definitions as defined by the language mapping; the importing module works with the internal representations of the imported definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:explicit-language-mapping
requirements.canonical: With an explicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions ARE mapped directly to separate TTCN-3 definitions, and the importing module imports the generated TTCN-3 and works with the mapped TTCN-3 definitions.
requirements.original: With an explicit language mapping, non-TTCN-3 definitions are mapped directly to separate TTCN-3 definitions; the importing module imports the generated TTCN-3 and works with the mapped TTCN-3 definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: In the first option, the import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool uses the internal representation of the implicit mapping of the module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.
requirements.original: The import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool uses the internal representation of the implicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: In the second option, the import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool imports from a TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.
requirements.original: The import statement imports the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool imports from a TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module's definitions according to the language mapping specification of that language.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: In the third option, the import statement imports the explicit TTCN-3 representation of the non-TTCN-3 module and the TTCN-3 tool imports the TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module according to the language mapping specification of that language.
requirements.original: The import statement imports the explicit TTCN-3 representation of the non-TTCN-3 module; the tool imports the TTCN-3 module which is an explicit mapping of the non-TTCN-3 module according to the language mapping specification of that language.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import statement SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and its TTCN-3 version is known.
requirements.original: a) The language specification should only be omitted if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and the TTCN-3 version is known.

ambiguity.issue: 'the TTCN-3 version is known' does not say by whom or how it is known.
readings: The language specification SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module is TTCN-3 and its edition is known to the tool (e.g. by its own language specification).
The language specification SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module is TTCN-3 of the same edition as the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:definition
requirements.condition: no other rules are defined in the respective language mapping
requirements.canonical: A definition imported from a non-TTCN-3 language source has public visibility by default, unless the respective language mapping defines other rules.
requirements.original: b) Definitions imported from non-TTCN-3 language sources have by default public visibility provided that no other rules are defined in the respective language mapping (see ETSI ES 201 873-7 [i.5], ETSI ES 201 873-8 [i.6] or ETSI ES 201 873-9 [i.7], respectively).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: The import mechanism IS designed to allow the re-use of definitions from other TTCN-3 editions or from non-TTCN-3 language sources.
requirements.original: NOTE: The import mechanism is designed to allow the re-use of definitions from other TTCN-3 editions or from other non-TTCN-3 language sources.

requirements.subject: ent:language-mapping
requirements.canonical: The rules for importing definitions from specifications written in other languages, e.g. SDL packages, MAY follow the TTCN-3 rules or MAY be defined separately.
requirements.original: The rules for importing definitions from specifications written in other languages, e.g. SDL packages, may follow the TTCN-3 rules or may have to be defined separately.

ambiguity.issue: 'may' could express a possibility for language mapping authors or a permission for tools.
readings: Language mapping specifications CAN define import rules that follow the TTCN-3 rules or define their own rules.
A TTCN-3 tool MAY apply its own import rules for definitions from other languages.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: A visible import statement of a TTCN-3 module MAY be imported by other TTCN-3 modules.
requirements.original: Visible import statements of TTCN-3 modules can be imported by other TTCN-3 modules.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of import statements has the syntax [Visibility] import from ModuleIdentifier [LanguageSpec] "{" import all [";"] "}" [";"].
requirements.original:
[ Visibility ] import from ModuleIdentifier [ LanguageSpec ] 
         "{" import all [ ";" ] "}" [ ";" ]

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing the import statements of a module re-imports the import statements of that module into the importing module.
requirements.original: This means that import statements of the module, from which the import statements are imported, are re-imported to the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: If module B imports the import statements of module A, everything that A imports using import statements visible to B IS also imported by B.
requirements.original: For example, if module B imports the import statements of module A, everything that is imported by A using import statements visible for module B, is also imported by B. If another module C imports all import statements from B, then C imports all what A is importing - provided that the import statements are visible to modules B and C.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import of import statements IS transitive: if module C imports all import statements of module B, which imports the import statements of module A, then C imports everything A imports, provided the import statements are visible to B and C.
requirements.original: For example, if module B imports the import statements of module A, everything that is imported by A using import statements visible for module B, is also imported by B. If another module C imports all import statements from B, then C imports all what A is importing - provided that the import statements are visible to modules B and C.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An individual import statement of another module SHALL NOT be imported; only all visible import statements can be imported.
requirements.original: It is not possible to import individual import statements of another module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import of import statements MAY be combined with imports of single definitions, imports of groups and imports of definitions of the same kind.
requirements.original: The import of import statements can be used in combination with imports of single definitions (see clause 8.2.3.2), with imports of groups (see clause 8.2.3.3), and with imports of definitions of the same kind (see clause 8.2.3.4).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Import statements SHALL NOT be imported from a non-TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: c) Importing of import statements is only possible from other TTCN-3 modules, i.e. the language specification (see clause 8.1) shall denote a TTCN-3 edition only, not a non-TTCN-3 language.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import of import statements SHALL denote a TTCN-3 edition only and not a non-TTCN-3 language.
requirements.original: c) Importing of import statements is only possible from other TTCN-3 modules, i.e. the language specification (see clause 8.1) shall denote a TTCN-3 edition only, not a non-TTCN-3 language.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module SHALL be compatible according to the rules of clause 8.2.3.8.
requirements.original: When importing into a TTCN-3 module, the language specification (see clause 8.1) of the importing module, the language specification of the import statement and the language specification of the source module, where the imported definitions are defined, have to be compatible according to the following rules.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.condition: a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition MAY import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists.
requirements.original: a) A TTCN-3 module of any TTCN-3 edition can import from a non-TTCN-3 language source provided that a TTCN-3 view for the non-TTCN-3 language exists (see clause 8.2.3.6).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: A definition or import statement IS imported according to the language specification of the module in which the definition or import statement is defined.
requirements.original: b) Definitions or import statements are imported according to the language specification in which the definition or the import statement is defined.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the defining module has no language specification
requirements.canonical: If the module in which the definitions or import statements are defined has no language specification, the language specification of the import statement that imports them IS used instead.
requirements.original: If no language specification is given in this module, the language specification of the import statement with which those definitions or import statements are to be imported, is used instead.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: both the defining module and the import statement provide a language specification
requirements.canonical: If both the module in which the imported definitions or import statements are defined and the import statement importing them have a language specification, these language specifications SHALL be identical.
requirements.original: If the module, within which the definitions or the import statements are defined, and the import statement for these definitions or import statements provide both a language specification, then they shall be identical.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: neither the defining module nor the import statement has a language specification
requirements.canonical: If neither the defining module nor the import statement has a language specification, the language specification IS determined from other sources in a tool-specific way.
requirements.original: If none of the two has a language specification, the language specification has to be known from other sources, which is tool specific.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT import from a later TTCN-3 edition than its own; it SHALL import only from earlier or the same editions.
requirements.original: c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement SHALL be lower than or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
requirements.original: c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: The rule is introduced with 'e.g.' although it restates the edition rule ('i.e.' seems meant); also the ordering of language identifiers is not explicitly defined.
readings: The import statement's TTCN-3 language specification SHALL denote an edition not later than the importing module's edition (comparison by edition date).
The comparison of language specifications is only one example; other checks of edition ordering may apply instead.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module MAY define other modules to be its friend modules.
requirements.original: Modules can define other modules to be friends.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module-declaration
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration has the syntax [private] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";".
requirements.original: [ private ] friend module ModuleIdentifier { "," ModuleIdentifier } ";"

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module-declaration
requirements.canonical: Friendship to modules IS defined by the exporting module, which declares the definitions, and IS NOT defined by the importing module.
requirements.original: Friendship to modules is defined by the exporting module (the module that declares the definitions) not by the importing module (the module that uses the module definitions of another module).

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module
requirements.canonical: Friendship between modules MAY be cyclic.
requirements.original: Friendship can be cyclic.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module
requirements.condition: the importing module is a friend of the exporting module
requirements.canonical: If a module is a friend of a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with `public` and `friend` visibility ARE visible to the friend module.
requirements.original: If a module is friend to a module from which it imports top-level definitions, all top-level definitions with public and friend visibility are visible to the friend module.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: For a non-friend importing module, only `public` top-level definitions ARE visible.
requirements.original: For non-friend modules, public top-level definitions are visible only.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module-declaration
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration that references a missing module SHALL NOT cause an error.
requirements.original: Missing friend modules shall not cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: 'Missing' is not defined: it may mean a module that does not exist at all or one that is not part of the current compilation.
readings: A friend module declaration naming a module that does not exist in the test suite SHALL NOT cause an error.
A friend module declaration naming a module that is not available to the tool in the current build SHALL NOT cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY check friend modules.
requirements.original: NOTE: Friend modules can be checked by tools, however at most warning are to be issued if a friend module is missing.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL NOT issue more than a warning if a friend module is missing.
requirements.original: NOTE: Friend modules can be checked by tools, however at most warning are to be issued if a friend module is missing.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module-declaration
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration SHALL have only `private` visibility, if any visibility is specified.
requirements.original: a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.

ambiguity.issue: 'friend definitions' is used for friend module declarations.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-module-declaration
requirements.canonical: A friend module declaration IS always private.
requirements.original: a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.

requirements.subject: ent:top-level-definition
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition HAS a visibility.
requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement HAS a visibility.
requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.subject: ent:visibility
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level module definition or an import statement MAY be set explicitly by a visibility modifier.
requirements.original: Top-level module definitions and import statements have a visibility, which can be explicitly set.

requirements.subject: ent:top-level-definition
requirements.condition: no visibility modifier is given
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition without an explicit visibility modifier IS public by default, except for imported definitions and friend definitions.
requirements.original: They are by default public except for imported and friend definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'friend definitions' (definitions with explicit friend visibility) cannot be default-public, since their visibility is explicit; the exception is redundant and the term is not defined.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: no visibility modifier is given
requirements.canonical: An import statement without an explicit visibility modifier IS private by default.
requirements.original: Import definitions are by default private.

ambiguity.issue: 'Import definitions' is used for import statements; elsewhere 'import statement' and 'imported definition' are used.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-definition
requirements.canonical: A friend definition IS private only.
requirements.original: Friend definitions are private only.

readings: A friend module declaration (friend module X) SHALL only have private visibility.
A definition with friend visibility IS not importable by non-friend modules (i.e. private towards them).
ambiguity.issue: Chosen reading: 'friend definitions' denotes friend module declarations (clause 8.2.4), which can only be private. The term is undefined and could be confused with definitions having friend visibility.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group definition IS public only.
requirements.original: Group definitions are public only.

ambiguity.issue: 'Group definitions' vs 'groups' in 8.2.5-s014; same meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: A group definition SHALL NOT be declared with `friend` or `private` visibility.
requirements.original: Group definitions are public only.

requirements.subject: ent:visibility
requirements.canonical: A visibility modifier HAS the syntax [ `public` | `friend` | `private` ], i.e. it is optional and is one of the keywords `public`, `friend` or `private`.
requirements.original: [ public | friend | private ]

requirements.subject: ent:visibility
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement CONTROLS whether it is importable by another module.
requirements.original: The visibility controls whether a top-level definition or an import statement is importable by another module.

requirements.subject: ent:visibility
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement IS one of three visibilities: public, friend or private.
requirements.original: Three visibilities are distinguished:

requirements.subject: ent:public-modifier
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility IS importable by any other module.
requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with public visibility is importable by any other module.

requirements.subject: ent:friend-modifier
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility IS importable by friend modules only.
requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with friend visibility is importable by friend modules only (see clause 8.2.4).

requirements.subject: ent:private-modifier
requirements.canonical: A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility SHALL NOT be imported by any other module.
requirements.original: A top-level definition or an import statement with private visibility cannot be imported at all.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-definition
requirements.canonical: When an importable definition is imported, all information of referenced definitions necessary for the usage of the importable definition IS imported together with it, even if a referenced definition is private.
requirements.original: NOTE: As specified in restriction e) of clause 8.2.3.1, this means that importable definitions are imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the importable definition, even if the referenced definition is private.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier of a private referenced definition IS NOT visible in the importing module.
requirements.original: Only the identifier of the referenced definition is not visible in the importing TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a group IS always public.
requirements.original: The visibility of groups is always public.

requirements.subject: ent:imported-definition
requirements.condition: no visibility modifier is given for the import statement
requirements.canonical: The visibility of an imported definition IS private by default.
requirements.original: The visibility of imported definitions is by default private.

readings: An import statement without visibility modifier is private, so the definitions imported by it are not re-exported.
An imported definition itself carries a private visibility in the importing module.
ambiguity.issue: Visibility applies to import statements (s003, table 10); chosen reading: the imported definitions are by default not re-importable from the importing module, as the import statement is private.

requirements.subject: ent:module-definition
requirements.condition: no visibility modifier is given
requirements.canonical: A module definition other than a group or an imported definition IS public by default.
requirements.original: All other module definitions are by default public.

requirements.subject: ent:visibility
requirements.canonical: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement DEFINES its importability by another module.
requirements.original: The visibility of a top-level definition or an import statement defines their importability by another module.

requirements.subject: ent:group
requirements.canonical: Membership of a top-level definition or an import statement in a group IS NOT affecting the importability of that definition.
requirements.original: If the top-level definition or the import statement is part of a group, this has no effect on the importability of the module definition.

readings: Group membership never changes the visibility/importability of the definition (a private definition in a group is not imported by group import).
Group membership has no effect on direct import, but importability via group import is still governed separately.
ambiguity.issue: Chosen reading: the visibility of the definition alone determines importability, including via group import (consistent with table 9).

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control part IS a shorthand notation to define a module control function.
requirements.original: The module control part is a shorthand notation to define a module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control part HAS the syntax `control` StatementBlock.
requirements.original: control StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: The module control part IS equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no `runs on` clause and no `return` clause.
requirements.original: The shorthand notation is equivalent to a module control function with the same statement block, no parameters, no runs on clause and no return clause (see clause 16.1).

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module CAN contain at most one module control part.
requirements.original: NOTE: As the control part is a short hand notation of a control function with the name "control", at most 1 control part can be defined in a TTCN-3 module.

readings: A module SHALL NOT contain more than one control part.
A module SHALL NOT contain both a control part and an explicitly declared function named control, nor more than one control part.
ambiguity.issue: The note derives the limit from the name clash; chosen the plain reading (at most one control part). Whether a control part plus an explicit control function is also forbidden is implied but not stated.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.canonical: When not used as an entry point for test suite execution, a module control function CAN be invoked explicitly like a function, using the `control` keyword instead of an identifier.
requirements.original: When not used as an entry point for execution of the test suite, the module control function can be invoked explicitly in a similar way as a standard function, using the control keyword instead of the identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:control-keyword
requirements.canonical: In an explicit invocation of a module control function, the `control` keyword MAY be prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.
requirements.original: In this case, the control keyword may be optionally prefixed with a module identifier followed by a dot.

requirements.subject: ent:module-control-function
requirements.condition: the referenced module control function does not have any parameters
requirements.canonical: If the referenced module control function has no parameters, the parameter list MAY be omitted at the place of invocation.
requirements.original: If the referenced module control function does not have any parameters, the parameter list may also be omitted at the place of invocation.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameter list' at the invocation means the actual parameter list (the parentheses).
